patch.value:
## User goal

An issue should be able to reference one relevant learning among hundreds on a feature, without retrieving the entire collection or losing the reference when another entry is removed. The requested capability is broader than learnings: a reusable public SDK reference/addressing primitive for item metadata, exposed ergonomically through CLI and other transports.

Do not assume every scalar field needs a generated ID. Distinguish field paths, stable collection-entry identity, and version-pinned historical references. The exact schema is an open design decision.

## Verified on published 2026.10.3

npm/tag commit: ca6e718707d7a1582f7abc437f5bd88aab156dfd. Isolated synthetic tracker, no real project data changed.

1. Create a Feature through `PmClient.create`.
2. Append two learnings through `pm.learnings(id, {add: ...})`.
3. The second add receipt reports `mutation_receipt.entry_index: 2`; the learning contains `created_at`, `author`, and `text`, without a stable per-entry ID.
4. Delete learning 1 with `pm.learnings(id, {delete: 1})`.
5. The target learning is now position 1, preserving timestamp/text but still without an entry ID.

The current CLI exposes edit/delete by one-based index and latest-N/full-history reads; the public options do not expose an entry-ID selector. The top-level result `id` is the owning item ID, not the learning ID.

An illustrative dependency target `feature-id#learnings/2` is rejected with `dependency_target_not_found`; this is not documented syntax and is included only to distinguish arbitrary fragment strings from a supported resolver. Generic in-memory graph node strings do not themselves provide persisted metadata reference resolution.

Sources: [LogNote and Comment shapes](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/ca6e718707d7a1582f7abc437f5bd88aab156dfd/src/types.ts), [shared annotation contracts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/ca6e718707d7a1582f7abc437f5bd88aab156dfd/src/sdk/annotations.ts), [learnings public operation](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/ca6e718707d7a1582f7abc437f5bd88aab156dfd/src/sdk/learnings.ts).

## Proposed acceptance

- Define a reusable SDK contract to address and resolve metadata fields, collection entries, and supported fragments; expose equivalent agent-oriented CLI behavior.
- Permit relationships/evidence references to target the specific referenced value, with owning item/workspace provenance.
- Collection-entry references remain stable when unrelated entries are inserted, deleted, reordered, or merged. Define edit semantics and distinguish live identity from immutable/version-pinned content.
- Selective resolution returns only the requested content plus explicit provenance/version and missing/deleted/ambiguous status, within normal output budgets.
- Preserve compatibility for existing `.toon` and JSONL history, including import, copy, restore, branch merge, and redaction. Do not silently reidentify old records or fabricate historical identities.
- Cover learnings as the concrete regression fixture and evaluate comments, notes, evidence and structured custom metadata without assuming they all have identical requirements.
- Keep primitives harness-independent and configurable; no per-learning bespoke command family or forced human-centric syntax.

## Scope and duplicate check

This is an enhancement grounded in a runtime identity limitation, not a claim that all metadata operations are broken. Searched open/closed GitHub issues and all-status tracked items for annotation identity, learning references, entry IDs, metadata addressability and fragments. Existing annotation output receipts, grammar consolidation, history reconstruction, and whole-item relationships are related but do not establish this fine-grained reference contract.

Related existing owner: [Storage, history and data durability](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/epics/pm-o2kc.toon). Please link a canonical implementation PM item during local-agent intake; no new checkout item was created here, preserving the active local writer's ownership.
SDK metadata reference primitive: stable collection-entry identity and selective fragment resolution

Provide a reusable public SDK addressing and resolution contract for metadata field paths, stable collection-entry identity and version-pinned historical fragments, with bounded CLI/MCP transport parity.

Define a reusable SDK address/resolution contract distinguishing field paths, stable collection-entry identity and historical version pins; expose equivalent agent-oriented CLI/MCP behavior.; Resolve only the requested content with owning item/workspace and version provenance plus explicit missing, deleted or ambiguous status within normal output budgets.; Keep learning-entry references stable across unrelated insertion, deletion, reordering and merge; define target edits and live versus pinned historical semantics.; Preserve old TOON and JSONL history plus import, copy, restore, branch merge and redaction compatibility without fabricating historical identities.; Cover real learning regression and evaluate comments, notes, evidence and custom metadata without assuming identical storage requirements; no per-learning bespoke family.; Permit typed relationships or evidence to target supported fragments while preserving whole-item compatibility and configurable harness-independent primitives.
Reference one relevant metadata value without retrieving an entire collection or confusing its mutable index with identity.
Stable, provenance-aware context references usable by every project domain and transport.
GH-1381 reproduced on published 2026.10.3 that deleting an unrelated learning shifts the target index; the universal SDK needs an explicit stable-addressing contract.

New GitHub enhancement intake: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1419 . Reuse this canonical stable collection-entry identity and edit-semantics feature; no new item or implementation claim. Full all-status corpus2901, request-specific searches, open/in-progress inventories and live full feature/predecessor reads find no separate in-place linked-test editor owner. The current runtime test contract lists add/remove/run selectors but no update selector. Repeated add-json for an existing command preserves the old note, as independently encountered in pm-gh1417 receipts. Completed pm-bjpo owns atomic whole-collection replacement, which differs from preserving one entry position and original provenance. Preserve existing replacement compatibility when designing the shared SDK metadata mutation boundary. The concrete report is retained below as proposed future acceptance; this feature remains open and unclaimed.

## Problem

A linked test's metadata (`note`, `timeout_seconds`, `path`, `scope`) cannot be changed in place. The only route is to remove the entry and re-add it:

```bash
pm test pm-github-9cjx --remove-index 1
pm test pm-github-9cjx --add-json '{"command":"npm run coverage","path":"scripts/coverage-gate.ts","scope":"project","timeout_seconds":900,"note":"Exact 100/100/100/100 gate …"}'
```

That has real costs for agents keeping trackers accurate:

- The agent must restate every field. A forgotten `path` or `timeout_seconds` is silently dropped.
- The entry moves to the end of `--list` order, so a later `--only-index N` or `--remove-index N` in a script or prompt now targets a different test.
- The original `provenance` (author, created_at, source_ref) is replaced by the editor's. The record of who linked the test, and when, is lost.
- History shows a removal plus an addition rather than an edit, which reads as a different test.

This came up in a code review: a reviewer bot flagged that a linked test note still said "this item remains open until it measures … exact 100" after the gate passed. Notes like this go stale whenever work completes, and every tracker hygiene pass has to work around it.

## Proposal

`pm test <id> --update <selector> --set note=… [--set timeout_seconds=…]`, or `--update-index <n> --note …`, that:

- edits only the named fields, keeping position and the original `provenance`, plus an `updated_by` / `updated_at` pair;
- records one `test_updated` history event with a field-level diff;
- refuses selectors that match zero or several entries, with the candidates listed (like `--remove`);
- has an SDK equivalent (`updateLinkedTest`) so extensions can maintain their own receipts.

## Acceptance

- Changing a note keeps the entry's `--list` index and original provenance.
- History shows a single update event naming the changed fields.
- An ambiguous or empty selector is refused, with no mutation.

Its exact API/schema is still a design decision. Completed whole-collection replacement pm-bjpo remains a compatibility predecessor, not an outstanding defect or an implementation of this proposal. No duplicate PM item, source change, claim or fabricated completion is introduced.
